title: Text Embeddings Reveal (Almost) As Much As Text
authors: John Morris; Volodymyr Kuleshov; Vitaly Shmatikov; Alexander Rush
objective: Reconstruct full text and personal information from dense embeddings
languages_scripts: English experiments in the reviewed paper; no BN/ROM/MIX reported
datasets_size_provenance_splits: Wikipedia 5M passages for GTR; MS MARCO data for OpenAI ada-002; Natural Questions, MS MARCO, BEIR out-of-domain; clinical notes for names; exact split details vary by experiment
victim_models_representation: GTR-base and OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002; sentence vectors; exact dimensionality/pooling configuration NOT REPORTED in matrix audit
attacker_access_and_method: Vec2Text base plus iterative correction/re-embedding; victim query access required
auxiliary_data: Large paired training sets; 5M Wikipedia passages for GTR setting; MS MARCO for OpenAI setting
metrics: Exact match, BLEU, token F1, cosine and entity/name recovery
findings: ACL abstract reports 92% exact recovery on 32-token inputs in its setting and full-name recovery in clinical notes
limitations: Input length and corpus/model-specific; requires query access for iterative feedback
relevance: Core query-access baseline; exact recovery distinct from entities
verification_status: Citation/method/dataset names verified; detailed per-run configs NOT REPORTED here

title: Sentence Embedding Leaks More Information than You Expect: Generative Embedding Inversion Attack to Recover the Whole Sentence
authors: Haoran Li; Mingshi Xu; Yangqiu Song
objective: Generate ordered text from sentence embeddings
languages_scripts: English benchmark experiments; no BN/ROM/MIX identified in paper audit
datasets_size_provenance_splits: PersonaChat: 162064 sentences, 82:9:9 split; QNLI: 220412, 95:0:5 split; reported average lengths 11.71 and 18.25
victim_models_representation: SBERT; SimCSE-BERT; SimCSE-RoBERTa; Sentence-T5; MPNet; frozen victim; embedding is projected into GPT-2 representation space
attacker_access_and_method: GEIA: train/fine-tune GPT-2 decoder from black-box sentence vectors; victim weights frozen; query/paired auxiliary access assumed
auxiliary_data: Auxiliary data distribution similar to target; exact training budgets not extracted
metrics: Token micro precision/recall/F1, NER and generation-related classification metrics
findings: GEIA outperforms prior methods on token metrics in reported settings; reports entity recovery on PersonaChat/QNLI
limitations: English and benchmark specific; token F1 is not exact text or semantic equivalence
relevance: Generative baseline; shows need for separate entity endpoint
verification_status: Metadata, datasets, models, splits, method, and metric verified from PDF; all pooling/dimensions NOT REPORTED here

title: Against All Odds: Overcoming Typology, Script, and Language Confusion in Multilingual Embedding Inversion Attacks
authors: Yiyi Chen; Russa Biswas; Heather Lent; Johannes Bjerva
objective: Investigate typology, script, language confusion in inversion
languages_scripts: 20 languages, 8 families, 12 scripts: Arabic, Urdu, Kazakh, Mongolian, Hindi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Chinese, Hebrew, Japanese, German, Turkish, Amharic, Sinhala, Korean, Finnish, Hungarian, Yiddish, Maltese, Meadow Mari; Bengali NOT included in this enumerated set; no Romanized Bangla or code-switch condition
datasets_size_provenance_splits: CulturaX; train 600K each for Hindi/Gujarati/Punjabi/Urdu and 1M for listed higher-resource train languages; 500 evaluation samples per language; additional eight languages are evaluation-only in main text
victim_models_representation: Victim multilingual-e5-base and language-specific GTR/AlephBERT/text2vec models; inversion T5/mT5; representation layer/pooling variants evaluated; dimensions NOT REPORTED here
attacker_access_and_method: Black-box encoder with attacker query access for iterative corrector; multilingual and cross-lingual trained inversion models
auxiliary_data: 600K–1M training samples for inversion model by language; 4 AMD MI250 GPUs and 56 CPU cores; some configurations four days; paper reports about 40,000 GPU hours overall

limitations: About 40,000 GPU hours; no Bangla, Romanized Bangla, or code-switch target evaluation; preprint status
relevance: Closest broad script/Indo-Aryan precedent; exact Bengali omission narrows but does not prove novelty
verification_status: Full language list, dataset, model family, access, resource scale verified; detailed appendices reviewed

title: ALGEN: Few-shot Inversion Attacks on Textual Embeddings via Cross-Model Alignment and Generation
authors: Yiyi Chen; Qiongkai Xu; Johannes Bjerva
objective: Align victim embeddings to attack space and decode with limited alignment pairs
languages_scripts: English, French, German, Spanish; no Bengali, Romanized Bangla, or code-switch evaluation found in paper
datasets_size_provenance_splits: MultiHPLT English for decoder training; mMarco English/German/French/Spanish for multilingual experiments; 150K decoder train samples; up to 1K alignment pairs and 200 evaluation samples
victim_models_representation: Victim T5, GTR, mT5, mBERT, OpenAI ada-002 and text-embedding-3-large; attack FLAN-T5 encoder/decoder; mean-pool last hidden states and L2-normalize attack embeddings
attacker_access_and_method: Black-box victim; paired text/vector alignment data from 1 to 1K; train local decoder independent of victim; one-step linear least-squares alignment
auxiliary_data: Single paired point yields partial attack; performance increases to 1K; decoder uses 150K public text samples
metrics: ROUGE-L, ROUGE-1, BLEU-1/2, cosine; downstream utility ACC/F1
findings: Reports cross-domain/language transfer and rising ROUGE-L with alignment data; claims specific to tested encoders/languages
limitations: Four language settings only; substantial decoder training and pretrained FLAN-T5; does not test Bangla/MIX/ROM
relevance: Current few-shot/access-budget baseline; importance of including 0/limited/paired data distinctions
verification_status: Citation, data/model setup, pooling/normalization, language set verified from ACL PDF
